methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Heirloom Carbon is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of nine private frontier-tech companies and one public comparable (Lnza), all operating in the Climate & Energy sector at similar or adjacent funding stages. Key private peers include Redwood Materials, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $150M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a typical Series B step-up multiplier of 1.9x, implying a valuation of $285M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M—yielding a median valuation of $1.0B and a range of $700M to $3.0B.

The triangulated valuation range is $242M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $642M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around capital intensity, technology risk, and path to profitability in the frontier-energy sector. The stage-progression method produces a more conservative estimate, while peer multiples embed significantly higher growth expectations. Key uncertainties include the durability of peer valuations amid energy-market volatility and Heirloom's specific competitive positioning within its addressable market.
